title: Long-wavelength density response and momentum resolution in strange-metal charge spectroscopy
abstract: Momentum-resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) on strange-metal Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) observes a broad charge continuum that is nearly momentum independent over an extended finite-momentum regime, whereas optical spectroscopy determines a metallic local conductivity. We analyze the long-wavelength response function that connects these regimes: the proper homogeneous bulk charge-density polarization. For any homogeneous $U(1)$-conserving metal whose longitudinal matter conductivity remains finite in the $q\to0$ limit at fixed nonzero frequency, the Ward identity gives $χ''_{ρρ}({\bf q},ω)=q^2\operatorname{Re}σ_L({\bf q},ω)/ω$. We then prove that any nonnegative normalized momentum-resolution kernel with a self-similar $q$-scaled profile, uniformly bounded second moment, and tight second-moment tails preserves this $q^2$ asymptotic behavior, changing only the prefactor. Consequently, a nearly local finite-$q$ continuum in Bi-2212, if continuously connected to a regular metallic optical limit of the same proper bulk response, is naturally described by a crossover surface $q_\ast(ω,T)$. The theorem is a constraint on the proper bulk density response, or on a positive $q$-scaled convolution of it; screened loss functions and surface EELS observables require the corresponding electrodynamic conversion before the constraint is applied.
summary: This work theoretically connects momentum-resolved EELS data with optical conductivity in strange metals by analyzing the underlying charge density response function. It proves that this bulk response must obey a universal $q^2$ scaling law as momentum transfer approaches zero. This constraint defines a crossover surface, offering a fundamental test for theories describing charge dynamics in high-temperature superconductors.
main_problem: The paper aims to reconcile discrepancies between charge dynamics measured by momentum-resolved EELS (finite momentum) and those from optical spectroscopy (local limit) in strange metals.
main_result: It proves that the proper bulk density response function must exhibit a universal $q^2$ asymptotic suppression at fixed frequency, which constrains how finite-$q$ measurements relate to the local optical conductivity.
method: The analysis uses the Ward identity connecting the charge-density polarization ($\chi''_{hoho}$) to the longitudinal conductivity ($\sigma_L$), and then proves this $q^2$ scaling holds for any non-negative, self-similar momentum-resolution kernel.
model_or_system: The study focuses on strange-metal cuprates like Bi-2212, treating the charge dynamics via the proper homogeneous bulk charge-density polarization function ($\chi''_{hoho}$).
key_observables: Proper longitudinal charge-density polarization $\chi''_{hoho}(q, \omega)$, local conductivity $\sigma_L(\omega)$, and the resulting crossover surface $q^*(\omega, T)$.
important_parameters: Momentum transfer ($q$), frequency ($\omega$), temperature ($T$), and the ratio of momentum-resolution kernel width to nominal momentum.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is a homogeneous, U(1)-conserving metal, and that the measured quantity can be related back to the proper bulk response via electrodynamic conversion.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the Ward identity linking $\chi''_{hoho}$ to $\sigma_L$, derives the required $q^2$ asymptotic behavior for the bulk response, proves this scaling is robust against realistic momentum-resolution kernels, and concludes by defining the crossover surface connecting different measurement regimes.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical constraint derived from fundamental symmetries (Ward identity) provides a powerful tool to test theoretical models of strongly correlated electron systems against disparate experimental measurements.
